about: Synthetic known-answer recall corpus for the #9281 release gate. Every drawer describes a fictional platform, Heron; no text comes from a live palace. Drawers are written in file order. A group's superseded drawer is the stale answer on its subject and must rank below the current one.

drawers.text: Status as of the spring cutover: the Heron ingest service deploys to region eu-west-2.
Decision: Heron ingest now ships every release to ap-south-1, replacing the earlier region.
Status: Priya Raman leads the Heron on-call rotation this week.
Owner ruling: Tomas Okafor owns the Heron pager schedule from now on.
Session snapshot: the Heron release freeze is in effect until the audit closes.
The audit closed and Heron merges are open again; the freeze is lifted.
Status: the billing service database connection pool size is 40 after the load test.
Decision: cap billing's Postgres pool at 16 connections so it stops exhausting the server.
Resume target: the nightly Heron backup job runs at 02:00 UTC on the scheduler.
Standing rule: Heron backups start at 04:30 UTC, after the batch window ends.
The Heron API is serving version 3.4.1 in production.
Rollout finished: production Heron API now runs 3.6.0.
PR 4410, the search index rebuild, is waiting on review.
PR 4410 merged; the rebuilt search index is on main.
Resume point for the notifier work: wiring the SMS retry queue.
Notifier workstream picks up at load-testing the webhook fan-out.
The archive-sync daemon installed on the build host is version 1.2.0.
archive-sync was upgraded to 2.0.3 on the build host.
The Heron search team is owned by Lena Fischer.
Marcus Bell took over ownership of the search group.
The Heron API rate limit is 600 requests per minute per tenant.
Heron logs are retained for 45 days in cold storage before deletion.
To rotate the Heron signing key, run keyctl rotate and redeploy the gateway.
The staging cluster is named kestrel and runs in a separate VPC.
Feature flags for Heron live in the flagd service and are edited through the admin console.
Customer exports are generated as Parquet files and delivered to the tenant's bucket.
The search service rebuilds its index nightly and applies incremental updates every five minutes.
Incident postmortems are due within three business days of resolution.
The billing service charges tenants on the first of each month in their local timezone.
Heron's mobile app supports iOS 16 and later, and Android 11 and later.
Grafana dashboards for Heron are provisioned from the dashboards repository and never edited by hand.
Secrets are stored in Vault under the heron/ prefix; no secret goes in an environment file.
The scheduler retries a failed job three times with exponential backoff before paging.
Load balancer health checks hit /healthz every ten seconds.
Database migrations run through the migrate tool in a pre-deploy step, never at application startup.
The design system uses the Inter typeface on an 8 pixel spacing grid.
Weekly planning happens on Tuesdays at 10:00 in the Harbor room.
Heron's error budget is 0.1 percent of requests per 28-day window.
Webhook payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the tenant's webhook secret.
The archive service compresses blobs with zstd at level 9 before upload.
The Heron API returns 429 when a client exceeds its quota, and clients should back off.
Application logs are shipped to the log pipeline through a sidecar container.
The gateway signs session cookies, and cookie names start with hrn_.
The production cluster osprey spans three availability zones.
Customer imports accept CSV and JSON uploads up to 2 GB.
Search queries time out after 800 milliseconds.
The mobile app's push notifications are delivered by the notifier service.
The office coffee machine is descaled every Friday afternoon.
